headlines.title: Critics blame Health Secretary RFK Jr. as U.S. loses measles elimination status
headlines.description: With over 5,000 reported cases this year and 10 deaths, the U.S. is facing a measles outbreak it hasn’t seen in decades. Politicians and public health groups are blaming Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for the W.H.O. revoking the nation’s measles “elimination” status. NBC News’ Steven Romo has more on how the country got to this point.

headlines.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status
headlines.description: The U.S. lost its elimination status, marking the end of decades of progress. The CDC now reports more than 5,400 cases. It can take years for elimination status to be restored. NBC News’ Erin McLaughlin has the story.

headlines.title: Measles Resurgence Costs US Long-Held Elimination Status
headlines.description: The United States no longer holds its measles elimination status, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century. It comes as the virus has continued to circulate for more than a year. NBC’s Erin McLaughlin reports for TODAY on what the loss of decades of progress means, who’s now most at risk and what it would take for the elimination status to be restored.

headlines.title: U.S. loses measles-elimination status, WSJ reports
headlines.description: The U.S. lost its coveted measles elimination status, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The Pan American Health Organization is scheduled to announce the decision after over 5,400 cases have been reported nationwide. NBC News’ Berkeley Lovelace Jr. details what it would take for the U.S. to regain its status.
